correctness.rationale: Unrestricted global optimality follows from conjugation-averaging convexity. The complete spectral decomposition gives eigenvalues 1, 1-na, 1-(n+2)a and 1-2a-b lambda for all nonzero backbone Laplacian lambda. Exact constrained Chebyshev minimax and a three-affine endpoint comparison determine the optimum. The C_n specialization uses exact sin formulas and the inequality sin t <= t; endpoints n=3,4,5 and all n>=6 are covered. In-package verify.py checks 43 full matrices, 43 LP benchmarks, 560 asymmetric feasible points, 3 rational exact spectra, and 6 holding-constraint clipped cases; the proof is independent of the tests.

originality.rationale: The 2004 FMMC framework and prior five-vertex special case, and the 2007 single-wheel and complete-multipartite reductions, are credited. The exact three-phase all-transitive-backbone double-cone optimum, and in particular the cyclic n>=5 apex saturation and gap comparison, were not found or implied as stated in the inspected sources. The proof supplies the extra antisymmetric apex eigenmode and constrained three-affine minimax; similarity searches are only supplementary. Residual specialized historical coverage is disclosed.

value.rationale: For a natural network architecture with two unconnected hubs, the theorem identifies three precise competing spectral bottlenecks and a sharp transition to saturated apex probabilities. It unifies cycles, triangular/rook graphs and further transitive backbones, corrects the tempting unconstrained Chebyshev allocation on clipped examples, and compares a new infinite cyclic family n>=5 with the published one-hub formula, giving twice the leading large-cycle spectral-gap gain. These are finite-step implementable optimal transition probabilities, not an arbitrary numerical table.
